fixtures.text: The maximal analytic Schwarzschild spacetime is inextendible as a Lorentzian manifold with a continuous metric.
The metric extends continuously across a non-trivial piece of the Cauchy horizon, so a proper future C0 extension exists.
fixtures.why: existence of a C0 extension is the negation of the class conclusion

fixtures.text: The interior solution is C^0-extendible but not Lipschitz extendible.
There is no proper future C0 metric extension of the maximal development.
The class definition fixes the extension regularity to C0 and leaves the genericity topology open.
The Cauchy evolution can be extended across the Cauchy horizon with continuous metric; this yields a conditional refutation of the horizon-localized C0 formulation.
The maximal development is future-inextendible as a C2 vacuum solution.
The spacetime admits a C2 extension beyond the Cauchy horizon, so the C2 formulation fails there.
The C2 formulation makes generic precise as an open dense set in a weighted C1 topology.
A C0-inextendibility theorem entails the C2 conclusion, so the C2 class inherits it.
fixtures.why: stronger C0 result supports the weaker C2 class

fixtures.text: The maximal development admits a conformal completion with a complete future null infinity.
There exist vacuum solutions with a naked singularity visible from future null infinity.
fixtures.why: naked singularity is the negation of WCC

fixtures.text: This entry records the status of the Kerr stability antecedent; peer review is pending.
Small perturbations of subextremal Kerr settle down to a member of the Kerr family, giving stability of the exterior.
fixtures.why: stability result contributes to WCC-side completeness

fixtures.text: The naked singularities of the self-gravitating scalar field are unstable, so cosmic censorship holds in spherical symmetry.
fixtures.why: instability of naked singularities supports WCC

fixtures.text: There exists a one-parameter family of continuously self-similar solutions that form naked singularities in the scalar model.
The numerical study finds a critical parameter separating black-hole formation from dispersion.
Subcritical data disperse and the evolution is complete; no singularity is visible from I+.
